Watch Time Stats estimates how much time you've spent watching YouTube, using the watch history in your Google Takeout export. It adds up your watch time, finds your longest binges and busiest days, and shows when you watch, with your top channels and most rewatched videos.

This is the first release.

## Which file to download

Both installers under **Assets** install the same app. Pick one:

- `Watch-Time-Stats_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe` (recommended) installs it just for you and doesn't need administrator rights.
- `Watch-Time-Stats_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi` installs it for everyone on the PC and needs administrator rights.

## What you need

- 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. The app uses Microsoft Edge WebView2, which comes with Windows 11 and up-to-date Windows 10; the installer downloads it if it's missing.
- Your YouTube watch history, from a Google Takeout export.
- Your own YouTube Data API key. It's free, and you don't need to set up billing. Your history lists the videos you opened but not how long they are, so the app asks YouTube.

The [README](https://github.com/jriiik/youtube-hours-watched#readme) shows how to get your history from Takeout and how to get a key, step by step. To look around first, click **Try with sample data** on the start screen.

## Installing

Your browser may warn that the installer isn't commonly downloaded, because it's new and unsigned. Keep it: in Microsoft Edge, click **…** next to the download, then **Keep**. In the window that opens, click the arrow next to **Delete** (or **Show more**), then **Keep anyway**. The builds aren't signed, so Windows SmartScreen may stop the installer with "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on (Windows Security → App & browser control), Windows blocks unsigned apps like this one and offers no Run anyway.

To uninstall, go to **Settings → Apps → Installed apps** (on Windows 10: **Apps & features**). The README explains how to remove your saved key and video lengths as well.

## Checking your download

This is optional, but do it before you run the installer. `SHA256SUMS.txt` holds a checksum, a long code, for each installer. Download it too, open PowerShell and run:

```
Get-FileHash ~\Downloads\Watch-Time-Stats_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe
```

For the .msi, use `Watch-Time-Stats_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi` instead. If you saved the file somewhere other than Downloads, change `~\Downloads` to that folder. The code under **Hash** should be the same as the one for that file in `SHA256SUMS.txt` (open it in Notepad). Capital and small letters count as the same.

## Privacy

- Your watch history stays on your PC. The app reads the file you choose; it doesn't upload it or keep a copy.
- The only thing sent anywhere is the list of video IDs, which goes to Google's YouTube Data API together with your key, to look up each video's length and category. There's no account, analytics or tracking, and the app's security policy only lets it connect to Google's API.
- Your API key is saved on your PC and only ever sent to Google.
- The video lengths the app looks up are saved on your PC, so the next run is quick. YouTube's rules allow keeping them for 30 days, so the app deletes older ones when it starts and looks them up again when needed. **Settings → Clear saved lengths** removes them at any time.

## Known limits

- The interface is in English only.
- If your Google account isn't in English, the dates in your history are read as well as possible, but this hasn't been checked against real exports yet. A video whose date can't be read is left out, with a warning. A history in JSON format avoids this; the README's Takeout steps show how to choose it.
- **Export CSV** and **Share image** aren't there yet.
- The builds aren't signed, so Windows and your browser warn about them (see Installing above).
